questions.question: What are the some examples of enriched foods and their benefits ? / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What are theexamples of enriched foods and their benefits? [K] / [CO1, CO4]Enriched
  • foods are products that have added nutrients to enhance their nutritional value. Common
  • examples include:
  • Fortified Cereal -Benefits: Often enriched with vitamins and minerals like iron, folic acid, and B
  • vitamins, which support overall health and help prevent deficiencies.
  • Milk and Dairy Products. Benefits: Fortified with vitamin D and calcium, promoting bone health
  • and reducing the risk of osteoporosis.
  • Bread and Flour-Benefits: Commonly enriched with iron and B vitamins (like thiamine and
  • niacin), which are essential for energy metabolism and red blood cell production.
  • JuicesBenefits: Orange juice is frequently fortified with calcium and vitamin D, aiding in bone
  • health and providing a non-dairy source of these nutrients.
  • Plant-Based Milk Alternatives. Benefits: Often enriched with calcium, vitamin D, and B12,
  • making them suitable substitutes for those who are lactose intolerant or following a vegan diet.
  • Infant Formula-Benefits: Enriched with essential fatty acids, vitamins, and minerals to support
  • growth and development in infants.
  • Nutritional Yeast-Benefits: Often fortified with B vitamins, including B12, which is important
  • for energy production and neurological function, especially for vegans.

questions.question: What role does surface tension play in the texture and mouthfeel of food products, such as dressings and sauces? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What role does surface tension play in the texture and mouthfeel of food products, such
  • as dressings and sauces? [K] / [CO1]Surface tension significantly influences the texture and
  • mouthfeel of food products like dressings and sauces.
  • Texture and Consistency: Surface tension affects how liquids spread and coat surfaces. Higher
  • surface tension can lead to thicker textures, while lower surface tension allows for smoother,
  • more fluid products.Emulsifiers, such as lecithin in dressings, reduce surface tension, promoting
  • a creamier mouthfeel and better mixing of oil and water phases.
  • Mouthfeel: The perception of mouthfeel is influenced by how a product interacts with the tongue
  • and palate. Lower surface tension can create a more uniform and pleasant coating
  • sensation.Products with high surface tension may feel more viscous or sticky, impacting overall
  • enjoyment.

questions.question: Write about toxic effects of some metals and chemicals. / [CO1, CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• Write about toxic effects of some metals and chemicals. [K] / [CO1, CO4]Toxic effects
  • of metals and chemicals can lead to serious health issues. Exposure can occur through
  • ingestion, inhalation, or skin contact.
  • Heavy Metals: Lead: Affects the nervous system, particularly in children, leading to
  • developmental delays and cognitive impairments. Chronic exposure can cause hypertension and
  • kidney damage.
  • Mercury: Impairs neurological function and can lead to tremors, memory problems, and
  • cognitive deficits. Methylmercury, a toxic form, accumulates in fish and poses risks to pregnant
  • women and developing fetuses.
  • Cadmium: Linked to kidney damage and bone fragility. It can also cause respiratory issues
  • when inhaled, particularly in occupational settings.
  • Chemicals: Benzene: A known carcinogen that can cause blood disorders, including leukemia.
  • Long-term exposure affects bone marrow and immune function.
  • Formaldehyde: Associated with respiratory issues and skin irritation. Prolonged exposure may
  • increase cancer risk, particularly nasopharyngeal cancer.
  • Asbestos: Causes lung diseases, including asbestosis and mesothelioma. Inhalation of asbestos
  • fibers leads to severe respiratory problems.
